title: Practice 6: Антон Чехов · История одного торгового предприятия

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Как, однако, они… толсто пишут! — ___ (пробормотать) Андрей Андреевич, почесываясь.
exercises.why: «The past tense is formed by dropping -ть from the infinitive and adding -л for the masculine, -ла for the feminine, -ло for the neuter, -ли for the plural … the past does not have special endings for each person, but shows the gender and the number.» — DLI, Lesson 36. From Антон Чехов, «История одного торгового предприятия».
exercises.context: «The past tense is formed by dropping -ть from the infinitive and adding -л for the masculine, -ла for the feminine, -ло for the neuter, -ли for the plural … the past does not have special endings for each person, but shows the gender and the number.» — DLI,…

exercises.q: Он ___ (собрать / собирать) все книги, связал их крепко веревкой и спрятал под прилавок.
exercises.why: The verb написать is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress). Both the imperfective and perfective forms of a Russian verb are to be memorized as a pair because there are no definite rules of forming one aspect from the other one: some twin-verbs differ only by a prefix in the perfective aspect; some have other changes: читать — прочитать, получать — получить. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 37.  ·  From Антон Чехов, «История одного торгового предприятия».
exercises.context: The verb написать is called perfective and expresses a single action with emphasis on its completion (either in the past or in the future, since the present tense deals only with actions in progress).
